learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the construction and operation of equipment specific to hydraulic and pneumatic actuation systems.
Knowledge and understanding of the theoretical bases regarding the regulation of characteristic parameters of hydraulic and pneumatic equipment.
Ability to analyze and apply theoretical knowledge to solve specific applications of hydraulic and pneumatic equipment.
Ability to recognize and adequately apply experimental methods specific to hydraulic and pneumatic actuation systems.
Selecting and analyzing specific bibliographic sources for hydraulic and pneumatic actuation systems.
Demonstrates autonomy in learning on issues specific to hydraulic and pneumatic actuation systems.

syllabus_topics: Introductory problems. Advantages and disadvantages of hydraulic actuation. Hydraulic fluids. Simple hydraulic diagrams. Calculation examples.
Volumetric pumps. Working principle and static characteristics of volumetric pumps. Piston pump. Radial piston pump. Vane pump. Practical calculation examples.
Volumetric motors. Working principle and static characteristics of volumetric motors. Rotary volumetric motors. Oscillating motor. Hydraulic cylinders. Practical calculation examples.
Pressure valves. Direct acting pressure valves. Pilot operated pressure valves. Normally closed pressure valves. Normally open pressure valves. Functions of pressure valves.

Distributors. Distributors with cylindrical spool in rotary motion. Distributors with cylindrical spool in translational motion. Flat spool distributors. Pilot operated distributors. Actuation of distributors.
Flow modulation equipment. Throttles. Flow-through throttle relation. Two-way flow regulators. Three-way flow regulators. Check valves. Functions of check valves. Unlockable check valves.

Auxiliary equipment. Hydro-pneumatic accumulators - Constructive types and particularities. Reservoirs - specific calculation and design problems. Filters. Methods for determining the degree of liquid contamination. Types of filtration. Types of filter elements. Pipes and fittings. Linear and local pressure losses in hydraulic actuation systems.
Pneumatic actuation systems. Advantages and disadvantages of pneumatic actuation systems. Specific calculation for pneumatic systems. Constructive particularities of pneumatic equipment.
General aspects of experimental research and testing of hydraulic actuation elements and systems.
Study of hydraulic equipment symbolization, through the study of simple hydraulic and pneumatic diagrams.
Study and plotting of static characteristics of volumetric pumps.
Study and plotting of static characteristics of pressure valves.
Study and plotting of static characteristics of throttles.
Study and plotting of static characteristics of nozzle-flapper type elements.
Study of the structure of the pneumatic positioning system with pneumatic axes.
teaching_methods: Presentation of experimental stands and methods

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)
Laboratory activity (including lab sheets and colloquium)

assessment_rules: Grading is based on the points and weights assigned to each activity. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. Conditions for passing include knowledge of conventional symbols for hydraulic and pneumatic actuation diagrams, understanding the construction and operation of hydraulic and pneumatic equipment, and knowing how to calculate characteristic parameters of hydraulic and pneumatic equipment.
